subject: ventures/uk-cis-deduction-refund-calculator
auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 112, see run record
professional: a UK accountant (ACCA/CTA) who files Self Assessment returns for CIS subcontractors; they check first that the refund is worked from the deductions on the CIS statements, then the 2025/26 bands, Class 4 rates and the gross payment turnover test

evidence.correctness: Recomputed by hand against HMRC 2025/26 rates (PA 12,570, basic band 37,700, 45% over 125,140, taper 1 per 2 over 100,000; Class 4 6% 12,570-50,270, 2% above): incomeTax(110000)=33,432, class4(110000)=3,456.60, incomeTax(150000)=53,703, sample bill 6,351.80 and refund 2,048.20 all match (node -e on calc.mjs). But compute() credited labour x rate against the bill and ignored the 'CIS deducted per your statements' figure: sample with deducted 7,000 still showed a 2,048.20 refund; the reclaim is 6,351.80 - 7,000 = 648.20. A wrong headline number on the tool's main job caps this at 2.
evidence.completeness: Invoice deduction, yearly bill, refund/balance, unregistered 30% cost, gross payment turnover test, statement mismatch flag, summary download and print all work (node --test 26/26; UI code read). The statement figure is collected but only used for a warning, not for the result.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 26 pass. Mutants: POA threshold 1000->10000 survived; 45% additional rate ->40% survived; Class 4 2%->3% caught. 2 of 3 survived.
evidence.craft: calc.mjs (108 lines) is pure, rejects bad input instead of clamping, names its source. Dense one-line findings and a cryptic gbp() formatter; '1,200' is rejected rather than parsed (message is clear). Acceptable.
evidence.claims: Page says rules were written without a live lookup and lists what is not decided; disclaimer and 'Not tax advice' in footer and summary (page.test.mjs checks). Minor: 'payments on account' is listed as not decided yet a finding states the 1,000 rule without the 80%-deducted-at-source exemption. llms.txt github.io links are rewritten at deploy (source-only, not filed).
evidence.fitness: Walked a registered subcontractor with real statements: they type the statements' total, the tool warns of a gap, but the refund shown is still from labour x 20%, so the number they would plan around is wrong whenever a contractor deducted a different amount, which is the case the field exists for.
evidence.domain: Rates and thresholds match 2025/26 (frozen into 2026/27). The departure: HMRC credits CIS deductions as shown on the contractor statements (CIS340, 'claim on what the statements show', which the tool itself says), not a recomputed 20% of labour. POA: TMA 1970 s59A and SI 1996/1654 also exempt where 80% or more is deducted at source; not modelled.

checks.what: income tax and Class 4 at 110,000 profit (taper)
checks.method: HMRC 2025/26 income tax rates and Class 4 rates, by hand
HMRC 2025/26 additional rate over 125,140, by hand
CIS340: the credit is the deduction on the statements; 6,351.80 - 7,000
CIS340: deduction excludes VAT and materials

checks.expected: no errors for invoice-only; errors for blank status and negative labour

checks.what: disclaimer, source and scope list on page and summary
'payments on account' listed as not decided
checks.observed: finding states a 1,000 POA rule anyway, without the 80% test

checks.what: gross payment turnover test 30,000 for a sole trader
checks.method: HMRC 'CIS: gross payment status' (net of materials and VAT)

defects.what: The refund (headline and table) credits labour x rate against the bill and ignores the CIS deducted the user enters from their statements; with statements of 7,000 on the sample, it shows 2,048.20 back instead of 648.20.
Tests did not pin the 45% additional rate or the 1,000 payments-on-account line: both seeded mutants survived.
The payments-on-account finding states the 1,000 rule without the exemption where 80% or more of the tax was deducted at source, while the page lists payments on account as not decided.

verdict: Rates, bands and Class 4 recompute exactly, but the one number a subcontractor comes for, the refund, ignored the deductions on their own CIS statements and used 20% of labour instead, so anyone whose contractors deducted a different amount saw the wrong refund. Two of three seeded mutants survived. Does not meet the bar; the refund fix and tests that catch both mutants are in this round's PR.
